original_question: Which autosomal-recessive metabolic disorder is caused by a deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes the formation of a thioester linkage between fatty acids and coenzyme A, and is distinguished from classic methylmalonic acidemia by the ratio of methylmalonic acid to malonic acid in blood plasma?

final_qi.question: Which autosomal-recessive metabolic disorder is caused by a deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes the formation of a thioester linkage between fatty acids and coenzyme A, and is distinguished from classic methylmalonic acidemia by the ratio of methylmalonic acid to malonic acid in blood plasma?
final_qi.search_keyword: autosomal-recessive metabolic disorder mitochondrial enzyme thioester linkage fatty acids coenzyme A methylmalonic acid malonic acid ratio
final_qi.long_answer: The autosomal-recessive metabolic disorder is Combined Malonic and Methylmalonic Aciduria (CMAMMA). It is caused by a deficiency in the mitochondrial enzyme ACSF3, which normally catalyzes the formation of a thioester bond between fatty acids and coenzyme A. This disorder is distinguished from classic methylmalonic acidemia by the unique ratio of methylmalonic acid to malonic acid in blood plasma.
